title: NTK-metric task codebook for low-interference shared updates
hypothesis: For task updates whose distinctions are low-rank in the pooled tangent-kernel metric, an NTK-weighted Mirror codebook will preserve heldout task quality with at least 25% fewer complete bytes than independent updates and lower task interference than Euclidean low-rank coding, while beating the native NTK-weighted factorization control.

world.teacher: three shared directions with one low-energy component; task covariance is anisotropic and pooled NTK defines metric

development.tuning: none; closed-form readouts and rank-2 SVD

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native factorization alias or any strict gate miss.

success_gate: PASS only if heldout normalized error <=0.02, complete bytes are at least 25% below independent updates, inter-task NTK overlap is reduced versus Euclidean rank-2 coding, and Mirror strictly beats native NTK-weighted factorization in quality/bytes.
failure_gate: FAIL if native NTK factorization aliases Mirror, quality/byte gates miss, or measured NTK orthogonality does not improve interference over Euclidean coding.
boundaries: Synthetic linearized regression only; no trained network or real continual-learning claim.
Task-specific readout codes are stored, so no unseen-task generalization is tested.
The teacher is deliberately low-rank in the pooled NTK geometry; generalization outside this aligned case is not established.
Fresh seeds stay sealed after alias or gate miss.

amendment_01.before_execution: Added before testing the explicit orthogonal-basis control; initial rank-2 screen remains unchanged.
amendment_01.reason: The registry hypothesis requires a measured NTK-orthogonal code/basis control, while rank-2 weighted SVD alone only tests metric-aware compression.
amendment_01.additional_control: Full-rank task-specific coefficient codes over an NTK-orthonormal shared update basis; compare against full-rank Euclidean orthogonal basis and independent readouts.
